Investigation + planning task (do NOT implement anything). Determine whether Nxeon can host Call of Duty private/custom-client dedicated servers, and if so, exactly how — a feasibility report + implementation plan.

Context: Nxeon (/opt/nxeon = prod, /opt/nxeon-staging = staging) is a game-server host. It provisions game servers as Proxmox VMs running a setup script per game family. Its one datacenter is Singapore, no GPUs. The owner wants to sell CoD private-server hosting (Plutonium and newer alternatives) if technically and operationally feasible.

The CoD private-client landscape (verify/update where you can): **Plutonium** (CoD WaW, Black Ops 1/2, MW3/IW5), **BOIII** (Black Ops 3 — big for custom zombies), the **X Labs / AlterWare** family (IW4x = MW2 2009, IW6x = Ghosts, S1x = Advanced Warfare, H1-Mod = MW Remastered), and **H2M-Mod** (MW2 Remastered — notable because Activision issued a cease-and-desist in 2024).

### Part A — Codebase feasibility (READ-ONLY, this is the core question)
Understand how Nxeon adds and provisions a game family, so you can judge whether a CoD private server fits the model:
- `lib/games.ts` — GAME_FAMILIES, GAME_PORT, GAME_DISPLAY, GAME_ART_SLUG (how a game is declared).
- `lib/game-config.ts` — per-family config schema/variants.
- `lib/game-control.ts` — the GAME_CONTROL spec (RCON, dataRoots, service hints) per family.
- The game template/catalog: `prisma/catalog.ts` and `prisma/seed-wave2-games.ts` — how a game's `osTemplate.setupScript` (the shell script that installs+runs the server) is defined. Read a couple of existing games' setup scripts (e.g. minecraft, cs2, rust) to see the exact shape (Docker? SteamCMD? systemd? a `docker run` line?).
- `worker/index.ts` — `wrapDockerGameService`, `provision()` — how the setup script runs and how the game port gets published/forwarded.

Then assess, for each CoD client (Plutonium, BOIII, X Labs family): can its dedicated-server binary be installed and run headless in a Linux VM via a setup script the same way the existing games are? Key technical facts to determine or flag for verification: (1) does the client's DEDICATED SERVER run on Linux (many run via Wine/Proton, or need a Windows host — flag this, it's the crux), (2) does it need the original game files/assets (which raises the piracy/asset-licensing question), (3) what ports/protocol, (4) RCON or console availability for the panel. If you can't verify a client's Linux-server story from knowledge, say so explicitly and mark it "needs live verification."

### Part B — Web research (attempt; may be blocked)
Try WebSearch for current Plutonium/BOIII/X Labs *dedicated server* setup on Linux, hosting-provider precedent (do other game hosts openly sell it?), and any 2025-2026 changes/takedowns. NOTE: this session's WebSearch budget may be exhausted (200/200) — if searches fail, say so and rely on codebase analysis + reasoned knowledge, flagging what needs a fresh-session verification pass.

### Part C — Legal/operational framing (honest, not a lecture)
One tight section: these are reverse-engineered clients in a legal gray area; Activision has issued takedowns (H2M-Mod C&D 2024). Note the reputational/IP risk, the fact that many hosts DO serve this category, and a recommendation on framing ("Plutonium/BOIII dedicated server hosting" vs "Call of Duty hosting"). This is the owner's risk decision — present the facts, don't decide for them.

### Deliverable
A clear report: (1) per-client technical feasibility verdict (can Nxeon's VM+setup-script model run it — yes/no/needs-Windows/needs-verification), (2) which one(s) to start with if any (BOIII custom-zombies and Plutonium are the biggest scenes — but feasibility governs), (3) a concrete step-by-step implementation plan IF feasible (what GAME_FAMILIES entry, setup script approach, port, panel integration would look like), (4) the legal/framing note, (5) what still needs live verification. Do NOT write any code or touch the catalog — this is go/no-go intelligence for the owner and me to act on.

# CoD Private-Server Hosting on Nxeon — Feasibility & Implementation Plan

**Verdict up front: Technically feasible for every major client, but it does NOT fit the existing one-click model cleanly.** The blocker is not Linux — it's *game assets*. Every current Nxeon game either bundles a freely-redistributable server (Minecraft's `itzg` image) or pulls the dedicated server free via SteamCMD anonymous login (Valheim, Rust, CS2, Palworld…). **No CoD private client can do either** — each one runs on top of the *retail game's copyrighted files*, which the customer must supply. This is exactly why the codebase already deferred DayZ ("its server needs a licensed Steam account", `seed-wave2-games.ts:2`). CoD is a harder version of that same problem.

## Part A — How Nxeon's model actually works (read-only findings)

The provisioning pipeline is uniform and simple, which is good news for extensibility:

- **A game = one row** in `prisma/catalog.ts` / `seed-wave*-games.ts` with a `setupScript`, plus four parallel map entries in `lib/games.ts` (`GAME_FAMILIES`, `GAME_DISPLAY`, `GAME_PORT`, `GAME_ART_SLUG`) and one `GAME_CONTROL` spec in `lib/game-control.ts`.
- **Every setup script has the same shape**: `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && docker run -d --name X -p <port> -v /opt/X:/data … <image>`. It runs via cloud-init on an **Ubuntu 24.04 VM** (base VMID 9000, `catalog.ts:11-17`). There is **no Windows base template** — all five bases are Linux (`ubuntu/debian/almalinux/rocky`).
- **`worker/index.ts:154 wrapDockerGameService()`** rewrites that `docker run -d` into a `docker create` + a generated systemd unit, so the panel's `systemctl start/stop/restart` works. Any script *not* matching the exact `docker run -d --name` shape is passed through unchanged — meaning **a non-Docker setup script (raw Wine + systemd) is fully supported**; it just won't get the auto-wrap and must define its own unit.
- **Port publishing (`worker/index.ts:676-721`)** reads `GAME_PORT`, health-checks that the port actually bound (`checkGamePortOpen`), then auto-creates a NAT forward. **UDP is a first-class path** — `udpAttempt()` (`provision-health.ts:162`) probes UDP via connected-socket ICMP-unreachable detection, already used by Palworld/Valheim/Bedrock. CoD's UDP ports work through this identically.
- **Panel control (`lib/game-control.ts`)** supports `rcon: "source"` (Minecraft/CS2/Palworld), `rcon: "rust-web"` (deferred), or `rcon: "none"`. Games with `"none"` still get power + world-backup (systemd + `tar` over SSH) — just no in-panel console/player list.
- **Customers already have SFTP + a browser File Manager** (`app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx:541 FileManager`, `lib/sftp.ts`, `SftpAccess`). This is the mechanism that makes CoD viable at all — it's how a customer uploads their own game files.
- **No GPU needed** — dedicated servers are headless/CPU-only, so the "no GPUs" constraint is a non-issue.

### Per-client technical verdict

| Client (game) | Linux dedicated server | Needs retail game files? | Console/RCON | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Plutonium** (WaW, BO1, BO2, MW3/IW5) | **Yes, headless via Wine** (`win64`); community install scripts + forum guides exist, "works perfectly fine headless, no UI" | **Yes** — copy `%LocalAppData%\Plutonium` game data from a machine that ran the updater | idTech/Quake **UDP rcon** (not Source RCON) → panel `"none"` at first | ✅ **Feasible via Wine** |
| **BOIII** (BO3, custom zombies) | **Yes via Wine**; installer repos (framilano/KhawanC) target "Windows and Linux" | **Yes** — must copy specific `.ff` fastfiles from owned BO3 files | idTech UDP rcon → `"none"` | ✅ **Feasible via Wine** |
| **IW4x** (MW2 2009, X Labs/AlterWare) | **Wine/Proton only — NO native Linux binary** (official docs confirm); Wine Docker images exist (`dobolinux/iw4x-server`) | **Yes** — owned MW2 2009 files | idTech UDP rcon → `"none"` | ✅ **Feasible via Wine** (Docker-Wine image available) |
| **IW6x / S1x / H1-Mod** (AlterWare) | Same Wine story as IW4x; AlterWare publishes Linux guides | **Yes** | UDP rcon → `"none"` | ⚠️ **Feasible but needs per-title live verification** |
| **H2M-Mod** (MW2 Remastered) | N/A | Yes (owned MWR) | — | ❌ **Do not touch** — Activision C&D Aug 2024, project shut down. Successor **HorizonMW** exists but inherits the direct-legal-heat lineage |

**The Wine caveat is the real technical crux, and it's manageable but not free**: none of these run as clean Linux binaries. Each needs a Wine prefix (`WINEARCH=win64`, `WINEPREFIX`, `WINEDEBUG`), i386 arch, and Wine's crash/leak behavior under a long-running server — messier to keep alive than a Docker `docker run` one-liner. Community Docker-Wine images (e.g. `dobolinux/iw4x-server`) partly re-fit it into the existing pattern, but they still need the customer's game files bind-mounted in.

## Part B — Web research (searches worked; budget was NOT exhausted)

- **Hosting-provider precedent is well established and open.** Commercial hosts openly sell it: **TLS Servers** (BO2 Plutonium), **Legion Hosting** (BO1 Plutonium), **getServe.rs**. So Nxeon would not be an outlier in the market.

- **Two bright lines Nxeon must not cross**: (1) never bundle/ship Activision game assets in a setup script or image — the customer uploads their own owned files; (2) frame it as **"Plutonium / BOIII dedicated server hosting"** (naming the community client), **not "Call of Duty hosting"** — using Activision's trademark as the product is what invites a trademark/DMCA complaint. This mirrors how existing hosts brand it ("Black Ops 2 Plutonium Server Hosting").
- **This is your risk decision.** The facts: real competitors sell it profitably; the tech works; the IP posture is exposed but historically tolerated for these specific clients; H2M shows the ceiling when a project gets too close to a *current-gen* store SKU. Given the recent security-audit note (unresolved DB Studio RCE gating a second hosting customer), it's worth deciding whether a legally-exposed product is the right thing to launch before that clears.
- **Product-market note (SGP-only DC)**: the Plutonium/IW competitive-MP scene is concentrated in NA/EU. Singapore adds ~150-250 ms for those players — fine for **BOIII co-op/custom zombies** (PvE, latency-tolerant) but poor for twitch multiplayer. If you launch one, **BOIII zombies is the best latency fit for SGP**.

## Recommendation & implementation plan (if go)

**Start with exactly one: BOIII (custom zombies).** It's the biggest custom scene that isn't latency-sensitive to your SGP location, and zombies has no official server path so demand is real. Plutonium is the obvious #2. Skip IW6x/S1x/H1x until BOIII proves the operational model; never touch H2M/HorizonMW.

Concrete shape of the work (nothing below is built — this is the spec):

1. **New family** `boiii` added to all five maps in `lib/games.ts` + a `GAME_CONTROL` entry with `rcon: "none"` (panel gives power + world backup, no console v1). `GAME_PORT`: `{ port: <BOIII UDP, ~27017 — verify>, protocol: "udp" }`.
2. **Setup script (NOT the Docker one-liner shape)** — installs Wine + i386 + the free BOIII server files, lays down `/opt/boiii`, and writes its **own systemd unit** (so it skips `wrapDockerGameService`, which is fine — that function passes non-matching scripts through untouched). It must **not** download any Activision asset. The unit starts *disabled/stopped* because the game files aren't present yet.
3. **Two-step provision (the key departure from every current game):** provision finishes with the VM up, Wine + server binaries installed, SFTP ready — but the game service down. The customer uploads their owned BO3 `.ff`/game files via the existing **File Manager / SFTP** into `/opt/boiii`, then hits **Start** in the panel. This means the `checkGamePortOpen` gate in `provision()` must be **bypassed for this family** (the port legitimately won't bind until the customer uploads files) — otherwise provision would (correctly, by today's logic) fail the order. Add the family to a "port check deferred" set, or the health check will flip the order to ERROR.
4. **Onboarding UX**: a clear dashboard panel — "Upload your Black Ops 3 game files to activate your server" with the exact file list — plus a legal check-the-box "I own a legitimate copy." This is the single biggest support-load and conversion risk; the whole product hinges on customers successfully copying the right files.
5. **Follow-up (v2)**: implement idTech/Quake UDP rcon (a new `RconProtocol` alongside `"source"`/`"rust-web"`) to light up console + player-tracking in the panel. Defer for v1.
6. **Marketing**: brand as "BOIII Dedicated Server Hosting (Black Ops 3 custom zombies)", never "Call of Duty hosting". Reuse the existing game-logo drop-in convention + `GAME_ART_SLUG`.
